title: Redis Pub/Sub for Real-Time Messaging
description: Use Redis Pub/Sub to broadcast messages between services, build live notifications, and implement event-driven architectures.

data.text: Redis Pub/Sub is a lightweight messaging primitive that lets one process publish messages to a channel while any number of other processes subscribe to that channel and receive every message in real time. It is not a durable message queue like RabbitMQ or Kafka; messages are fire-and-forget, and subscribers only receive messages while they are actively connected. For live notifications, chat, and event broadcasting, however, Redis Pub/Sub is fast, simple, and very effective.

Channels are identified by string names, much like topics in other messaging systems. Any client can publish to any channel without prior registration. Subscribers listen on one or more channels and receive every message published to those channels. Redis pushes messages to subscribers as they arrive, so latency is typically sub-millisecond.

data.title: No Message Persistence
data.text: If no subscriber is listening when a message is published, the message is lost. Redis Pub/Sub does not queue messages for later delivery. If you need durability or replay, use Redis Streams instead.

data.title: C# (.NET) with StackExchange.Redis
data.content: StackExchange.Redis provides an event-based subscriber API.

data.title: Node.js with ioredis
data.content: ioredis supports both callback and event-based pub/sub.

data.caption: Redis Pub/Sub topology with one publisher and multiple subscribers.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    P[Publisher Service] -->|PUBLISH| C[Redis Channel]
    C -->|Push| S1[Subscriber: Email Service]
    C -->|Push| S2[Subscriber: SMS Service]
    C -->|Push| S3[Subscriber: Analytics]
    S1 -->|Send| U1[User receives email]
    S2 -->|Send| U2[User receives SMS]
    S3 -->|Store| DB[(Database)]

data.text: Redis supports glob-style pattern subscriptions. Instead of subscribing to a single channel, you can subscribe to a pattern like user:* and receive messages from every channel that matches. This is useful when you want a service to listen to a family of related events without subscribing individually.

terms.definition: A named conduit for messages. Publishers send to channels; subscribers receive from them.
A subscription to a glob-style pattern that matches multiple channel names.
Publish/Subscribe. A messaging pattern where senders publish to channels and receivers subscribe to channels.

items.question: What is the maximum message size?
items.answer: Redis does not enforce a strict message size limit for Pub/Sub, but very large messages can degrade performance. Keep messages small, and store larger payloads in Redis or your database, sending only references or IDs over Pub/Sub.

items.question: Can I have multiple Redis instances for Pub/Sub?
items.answer: Subscribers only receive messages from the Redis instance they are connected to. If you publish to a different instance, those subscribers will not see the message. Ensure all publishers and subscribers connect to the same Redis instance or cluster.

items.question: Is Pub/Sub reliable?
items.answer: No. Pub/Sub is best-effort. If a subscriber disconnects, it misses any messages published during the disconnection window. For guaranteed delivery, use Redis Streams or a dedicated message broker.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Redis Pub/Sub provides sub-millisecond, fire-and-forget messaging.
Messages are not persisted; disconnected subscribers miss messages.
Use pattern subscriptions to listen to multiple related channels with one subscription.
For durability, consider Redis Streams or a dedicated message queue.
data.takeaway: Redis Pub/Sub is ideal for live notifications and event broadcasting where speed matters more than guaranteed delivery.
